A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChemGuide and the same molecular-generation research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original QM9 and GEOM generation experiments, molecular stability and property measurements, DFT validation, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds guidance-duration tests, AIMNet2 and evolutionary comparisons, and gradient-similarity measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 locally corrects the stated sampling procedure: the oracle gradient uses z'_t instead of z'_0, and final sampling uses the recomputed mean and covariance. The core architecture, objectives, and bilevel framework remain unchanged. These corrections do not establish that the implementation changed; the new evolutionary algorithm is evaluated as a comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions use QM9 and GEOM for molecular stability and the same molecular-property tasks. The added experiments vary guidance procedures, budgets, and comparators within this coverage; the existing noise and property-distribution-shift scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: v1's standalone stability experiments compare ChemGuide with unguided EDM and GeoLDM. v2 adds AIMNet2-based force guidance on QM9 and GEOM (Tables 10–11) and xTB-scored evolutionary search on QM9 (Table 12), substantially broadening the comparison to competing guided approaches.

E3.justification: v2 adds systematic tests using the last 100, 200, and 300 diffusion steps alongside the retained 400-step setting, across five guidance scales. New protocols include AIMNet2 evaluation on 500 QM9 and 50 GEOM molecules, gradient comparisons on 10 QM9 molecules, and evolutionary settings with variant sizes 3/5 and intervals 20/50. The original main experimental protocol remains intact.

E4.justification: New Appendix H.2 tests sensitivity to guidance duration; H.3 compares neural and oracle force guidance and examines their gradient alignment; Appendix I evaluates alternative evolutionary optimization. These substantially extend the existing skip-step, generalization, collapse, and clean-guidance analyses.

E5.justification: New Figure 6 reports mean and standard-deviation bands for gradient cosine similarities using 10 sampled molecules. Existing range bands and quartile plots are retained. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty or seed information for the benchmark tables.

E6.justification: Tables 8–12 add substantial results for guidance duration and competing optimizers. On QM9, reported force RMS is 0.0104 for ChemGuide, versus best values of 0.0110 for AIMNet2 guidance and 0.0109 for evolutionary search. Main-table results are retained, but most energy-above-ground-state entries in v1 Tables 12/14 become positive in v2 Tables 17/19, such as -0.0083 becoming 0.0083. The new GEOM comparator results use unequal sample counts.

T1.justification: Equation 15 corrects the second perturbation from +ζU to -ζU, eliminating the identical-term subtraction printed in v1. New Appendix F adds mathematical reasoning distinguishing classical SPSA from Gaussian random gradient-free estimation, including assumptions and Equations 19–21. This is a localized refinement of estimator reasoning.

C1.justification: v2 removes the introduction's claim that ChemGuide is the first work of its kind. The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims about improved stability, compatibility with existing guidance, and applicability beyond stability optimization.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking guidance duration to force optimization, AIMNet2's Hessian computation to memory costs, gradient disagreement to performance differences, and directional guidance to advantages over evolutionary search. It also explicitly qualifies the GEOM comparison because AIMNet2 uses 50 molecules versus ChemGuide's 500. Existing property–stability tradeoffs and limitations remain.

D1.justification: The anonymous implementation link is replaced by a named GitHub repository, also advertised on the first page. v2 documents AIMNet2's batching constraint and provides evolutionary-search pseudocode and parameter settings. The original hardware, runtime, and model-training disclosures are retained; repository contents were not assessed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for AIMNet2, evolutionary guidance, and broader conditional-sampling applications, including Anstine, Schneuing, Huang, Wu, and Zhao. Together with removing the first-of-its-kind claim, these additions modestly broaden and qualify the positioning while retaining the original related-work discussion.

P1.justification: Neural-guidance background moves from Methodology into Preliminary, and v2 adds an appendix contents guide, new subsection headings, acknowledgments, and publication-header edits. Most existing prose and its narrative order are retained, with localized wording and cross-reference changes.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the appendix's visual evidence with Tables 8–12, the gradient-similarity plot in Figure 6, and an evolutionary-algorithm block. Existing displays are relocated and reflowed, histogram labels are revised, and the regressor-noise caption now names all five properties already plotted in v1. The molecule visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important weakness in v1's stability evaluation by adding competing neural guidance and alternative oracle-based search, substantially strengthening the controls for ChemGuide's central contribution. Guidance-duration tests and corrections to Equation 15, Algorithm 1, and most energy-sign errors further improve the evidence and technical consistency. Unequal GEOM sample counts, limited benchmark uncertainty reporting, and residual sign errors still constrain some conclusions, but the overall gains are substantial.
